summary: This study retrospectively analyzed 98 patients (102 eyes) with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) whose anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapy was interrupted for more than 8 weeks due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The study compared the visual outcomes of these patients to a control group that received timely anti-VEGF treatments, using spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) imaging to measure central retinal thickness and anatomical characteristics. The results showed that treatment interruption was associated with worse visual acuity and a sustained negative impact on visual function one year later, with longer treatment interruptions linked to greater deterioration in visual acuity.
